title: then two weeks of the peace chants and the closing mantras of each Upanishad
word: then two weeks of the peace chants
hook: I will, then I have: a promise made at the door and kept at the end
carry: then two weeks of the peace chants and the closing mantras of each Upanishad
tomorrow: five years done. so where did the whole thing begin?

segments.voice: Then two weeks of the peace chants, day eight. Yesterday, the Isha's last lines: the golden lid lifted, and fire asked to lead by the good path. Today, the last of these peace chants, and a promise.

I'll call you back. I'll be there. I'll finish it this weekend. Promises in the future tense are easy to send and easy to forget. The Taittiriya Upanishad opens its first part with a chant full of them. When that part ends, the same chant comes back, almost word for word. Almost: the tense has changed.
screen: `I'LL CALL YOU BACK.` → `A CHANT FULL OF PROMISES.` → `THE TENSE HAS CHANGED.`

segments.voice: The chant is known by its first words, sham no mitrah. In plain words, it opens: may Mitra be kind to us, may Varuna be kind, and Aryaman, Indra, Brihaspati, and Vishnu of the wide strides. Honor to Brahman. Honor to you, Vayu, the wind: you are Brahman made visible. I will call you that. I will speak the right. I will speak the true. May that protect me. May it protect the speaker. Then the study begins. And when the first part of the Taittiriya ends, the chant returns. The same gods, the same honor to the wind. But now: I have called you Brahman made visible. I have spoken the right. I have spoken the true. That has protected me. It has protected the speaker. Om, peace, peace, peace. The promise made at the door is kept by the end, and the text says so out loud. Now look back over these chants. Saha navavatu asked for teacher and student both. Three shantis faced trouble within, from others, from beyond. Purnam adah kept the full full. Bhadram karnebhih asked for good to the ears. Apyayantu asked for strength and no turning away. Van me manasi joined speech and mind. The Isha lifted its golden lid. And here, a promise kept.
screen: `SHAM NO MITRAH: I WILL.` · `VAYU: BRAHMAN MADE VISIBLE.` · `AT THE END: I HAVE.` · then, large: `A PROMISE, KEPT OUT LOUD.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one promise you've made that's still in the future tense. Name, silently, what keeping it would look like; then the one thing most likely to get in the way; then when and where the first step happens. Give each a few slow breaths before the next.
The peace chants, and today sham no mitrah: I will speak the true, said at the start; I have spoken the true, said at the end.
Hold on to it: then two weeks of the peace chants and the closing mantras of each Upanishad: I will, then I have. The great sayings, done.

howItsDone: Sham no mitrah is chanted at the opening of the Taittiriya Upanishad's first part (the Shiksha Valli), and its past-tense form is chanted when that part is finished.

fork.setup: at the start of the season you told your team you'd keep a team journal. it's the last game, and you did. what does sham no mitrah suggest?

fork.reveal: the Taittiriya's chant says it out loud at the close: I have spoken the true. naming a kept promise is part of keeping it.

original.note: Sanskrit: may Mitra be kind to us; the first words of the Taittiriya's opening chant.

trapdoor: what you thought: the same chant, said twice.
what it means: a promise in the future tense at the start, and the same words in the past tense at the end: kept.
what a scholar hears: Taittiriya 1.1 (vadishyami, I will speak) against 1.12 (avadisham, I have spoken; tan mam avit, that has protected me).

chat.meaning: The Taittiriya's chant opens with 'I will speak the true' and closes with 'I have spoken the true', said aloud. Naming a kept promise is part of it.

sham no mitrah.meaning: may Mitra be kind to us: the chant's first words

Mitra.meaning: a Vedic god of friendship and agreements

Varuna.meaning: a Vedic god of the waters and of order

Vayu.meaning: the wind, honored as Brahman made visible

Taittiriya.meaning: the Upanishad this chant opens and closes

sources.ref: Taittiriya Upanishad 1.1 (sham no mitrah … ritam vadishyami, satyam vadishyami, tan mam avatu …) and 1.12 (… ritam avadisham, satyam avadisham, tan mam avit …)
